description_full: PC Connection, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides various information technology (IT) solutions worldwide. It operates in three segments: Connection Enterprise Solutions, Connection Business Solutions, and Connection Public Sector Solutions. The company offers IT solutions, including computer systems, data center solutions, and artificial intelligence; a portfolio of managed services and professional services; services related to the design, configuration, and implementation of IT solutions; and cybersecurity, digital workspace, modern infrastructure, multicloud, and supply chain and lifecycle solutions and services. It also distributes accessories, cable and adapters, computer parts, computers, conferencing and AV products, electronics, media and supplies, monitors and projectors, networking products, office equipment, power products, printers and supplies, servers and accessories, software, and storage products; hardware, including devices and peripherals; notebooks/mobility products, desktops, communication products, displays, and sound products; and cloud solutions. The company markets its products and services through its websites. It serves large enterprise customers; small to medium-sized businesses, including small office/home office customers; healthcare, manufacturing, and retail industries; federal, state, and local government; educational institutions, including K-12 and higher education; medium-to-large corporations through outbound inside and field sales, digital and web advertising, and targeted marketing programs to specific market segments. PC Connection, Inc. was founded in 1982 and is headquartered in Merrimack, New Hampshire.

financial_summary: PC Connection, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $2.0B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 9% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $58M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.78× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 57% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 3% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.15x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-8.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 62% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 8% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 18% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 27% and a beta of 0.81, it moves roughly with the market.
About $11.9M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.6x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 42% in the 2020 crash, 21% in the 2022 bear market and 77% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 6% below its DCF fair value of $84.62, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 38%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $61.59 to $124 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/E 19.5 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 11.6 vs 16.4, richer on P/FCF 34.4 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 89% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.9% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $91.00 on average, 15% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 8.8%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.13).
It runs a 15% gross margin and converts 2% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only 0.78x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 0.3% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $406.7M (20% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.7, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.8% over 3 years, 2.1% over 5 years and 1.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 2% of profits supports about 0.3% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Capex runs only 0.7x depreciation (0.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 4, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 18.8% on average.
Analysts expect 7.1% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 57.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 43%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (41 sales, net $14.9M sold).
It returns 4.6% a year to shareholders (3.8% in buybacks and 1.0% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 0.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 2,525 employees, each generates about $1.1M of revenue, 3.1x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 2.3% a year.
That works out to $23K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $2.5M (2x revenue per employee).
